constraint: Consent accept/decline is never a chat-rendered control actuated by channel identity alone
where: contract §6.1 (WidgetIntent: `requires: ConfirmationRequirement | null` — "non-null iff effect ∈ {REQUEST_APPROVAL, COMMIT}"; `capability` — "MUST be null iff effect ∈ {NONE, NAVIGATE, HANDOFF}") against §6.8 NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED, §9.1 ladder step 3, §11 Gate 4, INV-8
why: The consent split's entire claimed structural defence is unrepresentable in the contract's own type system. §6.8 says the eight NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED capabilities have HANDOFF as "their only legal intent" and that each "additionally declares required_verification: SESSION_VERIFIED | STEP_UP_VERIFIED". But a HANDOFF intent must have `requires === null` (so there is no `required_verification` field to declare) and `capability === null` (so there is no capability name to match against the list). Gate 4 compares `verification_level >= requires.required_verification` — vacuous when `requires` is null. Ladder step 3 fires on `requires.required_verification > verification_level` OR `capability in NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED` — neither predicate can evaluate true for a HANDOFF intent. So on a CHANNEL_IDENTITY channel (Telegram, push) both the floor check and the list check are inert for exactly the intents that carry consent and identity-unbind actions, and the landing surface is unconstrained (see the separate HANDOFF-target finding). The claim in the winner rationale that "a channel-identity tap physically cannot actuate a 152-FZ decision" is false as specified.
fix: Make `requires` (or at minimum `required_verification`) mandatory on HANDOFF as well as REQUEST_APPROVAL/COMMIT, and add a non-null `handoff_capability_ref` (registry key, non-actuating) so both Gate 4 and the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED predicate can evaluate. Add an invariant: a CONSENT_STATE or IDENTITY_BINDING envelope is refused at emission unless every intent carries an explicit verification floor of SESSION_VERIFIED or above and a resolvable `s/<shell_route>` target.

constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut; consent never actuated by channel identity alone
where: contract §6.1 `ConfirmationRequirement.required_verification`; §11 Gate 4; §9.1 ladder step 3; IA §4.1–4.2 (Notifications as a chat SETTINGS_DRAFT)
why: `required_verification` is a field the emitter authors onto the intent at mint time. Nothing in the contract binds it to the capability registry, to `AiToolPolicyService`, or to a risk tier — §6.8 says NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED capabilities "declare" it, i.e. by authorship. Gate 4 therefore validates the session against a number the mint path chose, not a server-derived floor, so the ladder's protection is only as strong as every future composer. Concretely: per-moment notification delivery preferences are communication-consent decisions (`Origin.notify_pref_key` is described as "the channel-consent key that gated this emission"), IA §4.1 explicitly says the Notifications surface "also is one, in chat" as a SETTINGS_DRAFT whose apply_intent is a COMMIT, and notification consent is not on the NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED list. A composer that declares `required_verification: 'CHANNEL_IDENTITY'` on that COMMIT produces a chat-rendered marketing/communication-consent control actuated by a Telegram tap, and it passes every stated invariant.
fix: Derive the floor server-side: `required_verification = max(registry.minVerification(capability), policy.minVerification(riskTier))`, computed at mint and again at Gate 4; treat any emitter-supplied value as a hint only (the same treatment already given to `authority_hint`). Classify every consent-bearing capability — including per-moment notification preferences — in the registry with a minimum of SESSION_VERIFIED.

constraint: No BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION; widgets are never a system of record
where: contract §5.2 FORM row ("effect ceiling DRAFT / COMMIT"); §5.2 B2; §6.1 `InputSchema`; §11 Gate 12; §7 taxonomy (FORM owners include `loyalty.internal.adjust`)
why: FORM is the one kind that accepts free-form, non-domain-closed input (`string`, `number`, `date`, `time`, `phone` with only length/pattern caps) and it may carry a COMMIT for an inherited capability. The taxonomy names `loyalty.internal.adjust` and `expenses.create` as FORM owners. A FORM tap therefore delivers a client-authored magnitude straight into Gate 12 as "resolved arguments" — a direct business mutation whose value the user supplied. The two headline safety mechanisms do not cover it: handles-as-nouns protects `frozen_nouns` only, and `inputs` are values by construction; the closed `selection_domain` applies only to `enum`/`ref`. The only control is the `FormJustification` enum, which §5.2 B2 itself concedes is "a social control, not a technical one". The contract's claim that "a widget cannot express a direct business mutation" is therefore false for the single largest mutation surface it defines.
fix: Cap FORM at DRAFT: a FORM submission produces a server-owned draft that is re-rendered as a confirmation body (BOOKING_CONFIRMATION / SETTINGS_DRAFT / a new VALUE_CONFIRMATION), and only that body may carry the COMMIT — the same non-existence argument already used for booking. Additionally require every numeric/financial FORM field to name a server-side bound (min/max/allowed-delta) drawn from the capability, so a client-supplied magnitude is validated against canonical policy rather than a regex.

constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect; widget click cannot bypass booking intent, B31/B32/B33 or verified Client authority
where: contract INV-7 ("Action Engine ingress refuses non-confirmation sources for `appointments.own.create`"); §5.2 BOOKING_CONFIRMATION body; §6.4 I2(b); §5 Table A row 5
why: The enforcement clause that makes I2(b) real names exactly one capability: `appointments.own.create`. The registry also exposes `appointments.own.reschedule` and `appointments.own.cancel`, which are booking effects by any reading. INV-7 permits a COMMIT token to exist on APPROVAL, SETTINGS_DRAFT and FORM bodies, and nothing refuses a reschedule or cancel COMMIT minted on one of those. Since §11 Gate 11 states B31/B32/B33 run inside the booking owner's DRAFT step, a reschedule COMMIT that never passes through a canonical draft never runs booking-intent normalization, Client-principal verification or confirmation identity. Worse, BOOKING_CONFIRMATION's body has no shape for cancelling an existing appointment (its `cancel_intent` cancels the draft, not the record), so cancellation has no legal confirmation home at all and must be minted somewhere INV-7's clause does not guard.
fix: Extend the Action Engine ingress refusal to the whole `appointments.own.*` family and to any capability the registry marks as booking-class, keyed off a `booking_effect: true` registry flag rather than a hardcoded name. Add an explicit cancellation/reschedule confirmation body (or a `confirmation_subject: 'create'|'reschedule'|'cancel'` discriminator on BOOKING_CONFIRMATION) so every booking effect has exactly one canonical confirmation surface.

constraint: No BUTTON -> PROVIDER directly; the provider owner alone touches the provider
where: taxonomy §5 Table A row 22 and §6 (`PAYMENT_HANDOFF`, owner "`p4-06-yookassa-checkout-provider`, `gift-certificate-*-shadow` — shadow, not registered"; "Tips resolve through the native bridge", `MayaRuntime.openTipsURL`); contract §6 EffectClass HANDOFF; §11 Gate 11 ("HANDOFF -> signed deep link, no capability invoked")
why: PAYMENT_HANDOFF's declared ceiling is HANDOFF, and HANDOFF terminates at Gate 11 without invoking a capability and without ever reaching Gate 12, where §11 states "The Action Engine — never the widget, chat or renderer — calls the provider owner". The tap's destination is a payment provider's checkout, or `MayaRuntime.openTipsURL` on the native bridge. That is a widget button reaching an external provider with no capability, no Action Engine, no `idempotency_key`, no receipt and no canonical owner — and the taxonomy is explicit that the owner is unregistered/shadow. Because HANDOFF intents are capability-null, INV-10's registry check is vacuous and P2 ('no button for a capability with no canonical owner') cannot fire either, so an unowned money path passes every invariant. The project's own documented double-payment gotcha is exactly the failure mode an idempotency-free provider handoff reproduces.
fix: Do not model payment as HANDOFF-to-provider. Route it as a canonical capability: a DRAFT owned by a registered payment/commerce owner produces a confirmation body, the COMMIT reaches Gate 12, and the Action Engine (not the renderer, not the native bridge) initiates the provider session and owns the idempotency key and the receipt. Until `GAP-COMMERCE-GIFT` and the tips owner are registered, PAYMENT_HANDOFF must emit a LIMITATION with `capability_gap_ref` and no intent, per P2.

constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut
where: contract §6 EffectClass NAVIGATE/HANDOFF; §11 Gate 11; §7 `Presentation.fullscreen_detail.route_key`; IA §6 (four link classes)
why: The contract has no field anywhere that names a NAVIGATE or HANDOFF target and no invariant that constrains it. IA §6 defines four link classes but never binds intent targets to them, and one of those classes — `…/c/<capability_key>?scope=…` — is defined as "exactly equivalent to typing the utterance", i.e. it invokes a capability. So a capability-null NAVIGATE or HANDOFF intent can carry a `c/` link and thereby invoke a capability that INV-6, INV-10 and Gate 6 all believe does not exist for that intent, because the contract validated `capability === null`. The link is also the escape hatch for the consent HANDOFF: nothing requires it to resolve to `s/<shell_route>` (the only class with a stated SESSION_VERIFIED floor).
fix: Add a required, closed-shape `target` to NAVIGATE and HANDOFF intents — `{ class: 'w'|'i'|'c'|'s', ref }` — validate at emission that `c` targets are registry keys within the principal's authority and that consent/identity handoffs use `s` only, and log the class in RenderReceipt. Add an invariant: no intent may carry a free-form URL.

constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut; no BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION
where: IA §5.4 (six overlays re-expressed: `detail.cash.declaration`, `detail.expenses.intake`, four `detail.settings.*`); IA §5.1–5.2; contract §7 `fullscreen_detail`
why: Fullscreen details are entered by a capability-null NAVIGATE and then are governed by nothing in this contract — no envelope, no intent tokens, no gates, no RenderReceipt. Yet the details enumerated are precisely the mutating surfaces: cash declaration, expense intake ("correction"), and four governed-settings editors. IA §5.2 even states a detail may change something and post a receipt line back into the timeline, conceding they cause effects. The design's own diagnosis of these overlays is that "their only authorisation is the bearer check inside each component's first fetch"; moving the mount from a query parameter into the router removes the URL-as-authorisation defect but leaves the effect path entirely unspecified, so the mandated command path holds for widgets and is simply undefined where the business mutations actually live. The same applies to `SETTINGS_DRAFT.editor_handoff_intent`, the mandated non-chat fallback editor, which is a NAVIGATE into an ungoverned editor with COMMIT-equivalent power.
fix: State normatively that a fullscreen detail is a renderer of envelopes, not a second application: every mutating control inside a detail must be an intent from an envelope minted for that route, submitted through the same gateway and the same twelve gates. Add an invariant that no detail route may hold provider credentials, compose provider arguments, or call a business endpoint directly, and require details to declare their `source_capability` the way projectors do.

constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect; no shortcut from UI event to canonical owner
where: contract §9.1 ladder step 8 (NOTIFICATION: "a COMMIT action is permitted only when risk_tier === 'low_write' && reversible === true") against §13 ("A COMMIT reachable in one tap from a selector, a push, or a spoken utterance without readback" is forbidden); §5.2 APPROVAL row
why: The ladder permits and §13 forbids the same thing; as written, the permissive rule is the operative one because the ladder is what the server executes. A push action id is the intent token, so the path is tap -> gateway -> COMMIT -> Action Engine with no confirmation body rendered and no readback required (`requires_readback` is an authored flag, and step 8 does not demand it). The actuating principal is a device holding a push subscription — CHANNEL_IDENTITY. Because INV-7 confines COMMIT tokens to four kinds, the push card in question is most plausibly an APPROVAL, whose own safeguard — "consent-aware audience maths shown before the irreversible tap" — cannot be delivered inside the profile's own `max_body_chars: ~120`. The safeguard is structurally undeliverable in the one channel where the one-tap commit is permitted.
fix: Delete the COMMIT exception from ladder step 8: NOTIFICATION profiles carry NAVIGATE and HANDOFF only, landing on the confirmation body inside a verified surface (the rule IA §6 already states for link carriers — "an intent carrier never fires on open"). If a low-risk reversible one-tap action is genuinely wanted, give it its own effect class with a server-derived floor, a mandatory audience_size of null, and an explicit registry opt-in per capability.

constraint: UI EVENT -> TYPED USER INTENT -> AUTHORITY VALIDATION -> CANONICAL OWNER with no shortcut
where: contract §5.2 PROGRESS row ("effect ceiling NONE + cancel"); §6 EffectClass NONE ("dismiss, expand, local"); §11 routing map (cancel -> `POST /api/orchestration/runs/:id/cancel`); INV-6
why: Cancel is classed under an effect ceiling of NONE, which the contract defines as purely local and which INV-6 forces to `capability === null`. But the routing map sends it to a server endpoint that terminates a run and, via `runs/:id/cancel`, can abort in-flight execution. A server state change is therefore travelling under the one effect class exempt from the registry lookup (INV-10), from `maxSideEffectClass`, and from any capability-keyed authority derivation at Gate 6. Anyone who can replay a token for a widget they can see can stop another principal's run, bounded only by Gate 3's principal binding. The same mis-classification pattern applies to any future 'local' action that turns out to hit an endpoint.
fix: Introduce a `CONTROL` effect class (or class cancel as REFINE) that carries a registry capability and is subject to Gate 6 and INV-10, and reserve NONE for intents whose handler is provably client-side (no gateway submission at all). Add an invariant: an intent with `effect: 'NONE'` may not appear in the routing map.

constraint: Conversation history is never business/consent/booking state; UI event -> typed intent -> authority validation ordering
where: contract §11 Gate 7 (lowering appends the utterance to the conversation) placed before Gate 9 (input validation and noun resolution)
why: The lowered utterance is `render(utterance_template, selected labels)` with `{{selection}}` interpolated from the client's `inputs`, and it is written into the durable conversation as a USER turn before Gate 9 validates those inputs against `input_schema` (closed-enum membership, length, byte caps, `SECURE_SURFACE_ONLY` rejection). So input that Gate 9 will refuse — oversize, out-of-domain, or a `SECURE_SURFACE_ONLY` value the contract says must never be rendered in chat — has already been persisted into the transcript and, per C9Context, into the LLM's untrusted-text channel. With FORM's free-form fields this is a durable prompt-injection and PII-leak path into history that survives the refusal.
fix: Move input validation and `SECURE_SURFACE_ONLY` rejection to before lowering (validate at Gate 5/6, lower at Gate 8/9), and lower only from server-side canonical labels resolved from the closed domain, never from raw client bytes.

constraint: LLM never generates numbers for a chart; charts render canonical C7/C8 data
where: contract §4.3 `Provenance.generated_by: 'canonical'` ("No body field is LLM-authored") against §7 R2 ("Prose in text_equivalent, speech.lead and REPORT.narrative may be model-composed"); §5.2 REPORT body `sections[].narrative`; §5.1 `Measure.basis`, `Cell.label`; INV-14
why: Three defects compound. (1) The contract asserts a literal, `generated_by: 'canonical'`, glossed as "No body field is LLM-authored", and then permits `REPORT.sections[].narrative` — a body field — to be model-composed; the literal is therefore false and INV-17 enforces a false statement. (2) The numeral check is circular where it matters: `Cell.label` and `Measure.basis` are free strings inside the body, so a numeral a model put into a label trivially "maps to a Measure present in the body" and passes INV-14 while being model-authored. (3) The check is a numeral check, so quantities written in words ("выручка выросла вдвое", "треть клиентов") evade it entirely — and the design's own open question proposes whitelisting ordinals and compound tokens such as 'топ-3' and '2 из 4' to avoid false positives, which widens the same exemption.
fix: Drop the `generated_by: 'canonical'` literal or scope it honestly to non-narrative fields. Mint `Cell.label` and `Measure.basis` from the server formatter like `text_equivalent` and cover them by `body_hash`. Constrain model-composed narrative to a template with named `Measure` slots so quantities cannot be free text, and extend the CI check to a word-number lexicon rather than a numeral regex.

constraint: LLM never generates numbers for a chart; charts render canonical C7/C8 data
where: contract §5.2 CHART body: `series:{series_id;label;points:{x;y:Measure}[]}`
why: `y` is a `Measure` and therefore inside the Cell/provenance/formatter discipline; `x` is untyped and is neither a Cell nor a Measure. Axis positions, bucket boundaries and category values are chart numbers, and as specified they carry no `state`, no `as_of`, no `evidence_refs`, no basis and no coverage by R2's formatter rule — while `axes.x.type` is only a type hint. Nothing in the contract stops `x` values from being composed rather than read from the C7/C8 dataset, and `rows_digest` digests the dataset, not the rendered points.
fix: Type `points[].x` as `Cell<string | number>` (or a `Measure` where numeric) and extend INV-14's hash check to assert that the emitted series — both axes — reduce to `dataset_ref` + `rows_digest`, so a chart that does not derive from the canonical dataset cannot be emitted.

constraint: Widget click cannot bypass verified Client authority or the canonical owner; no BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION
where: contract §10 ("What a submission cannot contain: ... a record id, a price, a date, a staff id, a client id") and §13, against §6.1 `InputSchema.fields.type: 'enum'|'ref'|'string'|'integer'|'date'|'time'|'phone'|'boolean'` where `enum_values` exists only for `enum` and `ref`
why: The contract states as a guarantee that a submission cannot contain a date, a price or free values, and then defines an input schema that accepts `date`, `time`, `integer`, `string` and `phone` with no closed domain — only length, pattern and byte caps. The guarantee is true for `enum`/`ref` and false for everything else. Reviewers and implementers reading §10/§13 will conclude that Gate 9's closed-domain check covers all inputs and will not add value-range validation for the types that carry the risk (an integer for a loyalty adjustment, a datetime for a reschedule, a phone for an identity correction).
fix: Rewrite the guarantee to what is actually enforced ("a submission may carry only values drawn from a server-declared closed domain, or scalars within server-declared bounds"), and require every non-enum field to carry server-declared bounds (`min`/`max`, allowed window, canonical normalizer) validated at Gate 9 against the capability, not against a regex.

constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect; widget click cannot bypass booking intent or the provider owner
where: taxonomy §7 refusals ("Drag-to-reschedule is `SCHEDULE` + a `DRAFT` intent, not a new kind") against §5 Table A row 6 and contract §5.2 SCHEDULE row (effect ceiling `REFINE / NAVIGATE`)
why: Two normative statements in the same document conflict about the highest effect a SCHEDULE may mint. If the ceiling table wins, the taxonomy's stated resolution for the entire calendar/journal family is unimplementable; if the taxonomy note wins, a drag gesture on a schedule grid mints a DRAFT whose new start time is a client-supplied `time` input with no closed domain (see the InputSchema finding), against `appointments.own.reschedule`, which INV-7's enforcement clause does not cover. An unresolved contradiction on an effect ceiling is exactly the kind of ambiguity that gets resolved at implementation time in favour of the feature.
fix: Resolve explicitly in the contract: SCHEDULE stays at REFINE/NAVIGATE, and a drag emits a REFINE that returns a BOOKING_CONFIRMATION (reschedule variant) produced by the canonical booking owner with B31/B32/B33 run, on which alone the COMMIT is minted. Record the resolution in both the ceiling table and the taxonomy refusal row.

constraint: Conversation history is never business state; widgets are never a system of record
where: contract §8 ("Cross-channel resolution … Resolving in any channel resolves all"; `proactive_once`: "once acted on, resolved (\"Приду ✓\")"); `Lifecycle.resolution`; INV-11
why: `resolution.state` lives in the envelope — the presentation layer. For `appointment_reminder`, INV-11 caps a proactive envelope at DRAFT, so a client tapping "Приду" produces no COMMIT and therefore no Action Engine receipt (§10 `action_receipt_ref` is null outside a canonical action). The design names no canonical owner for attendance confirmation. The only durable record that the client confirmed is `Lifecycle.resolution.state = 'resolved'` on the widget, which INV-15 then guarantees is deleted with conversation history. A staff member reading "клиент подтвердил" is reading widget state as business truth, and history erasure destroys it — the precise pattern the constraint forbids.
fix: Either name a canonical owner for attendance/acknowledgement (an appointment-confirmation capability whose receipt is the record, with the envelope merely projecting it), or state normatively that `resolution` is delivery/presentation bookkeeping only and forbid any surface from presenting it as a client commitment. Cross-channel dedupe should resolve the *delivery*, not the business fact.

constraint: Conversation history is never consent state; deleting history must leave canonical records correct (and must keep the erasure promise it makes)
where: contract §8 Delete ("It never touches IntentRecords, Action Engine receipts …"); §6.2 `IntentRecord.utterance_template`; §10 `WidgetIntentSubmission.spoken_transcript` ("voice only, for audit"); §4.4 `GAP-HISTORY-ERASE`
why: The contract presents "erasure never touches IntentRecords" as a safety guarantee, but IntentRecord and the submission record hold conversation-derived content: the `utterance_template` (the sentence the user is treated as having said), the selected labels interpolated into it, and the full `spoken_transcript` of voice turns. After a user exercises the right to erasure over conversation content, their utterances and voice transcripts remain, keyed to `principal_proof_hash`. That converts a stated 152-FZ capability into a promise the system does not keep — structurally the same defect as `/unsubscribe` promising a revocation that does not exist, which §4.4 exists to prevent.
fix: Classify IntentRecord fields explicitly: authority-and-audit fields (hashes, capability, effect, timestamps, receipt refs) are retained; content fields (`utterance_template` renderings, selected labels, `spoken_transcript`) are conversation content and are erased or tombstoned with it. State the retention split in the contract before any erasure control is offered, and make it part of the `GAP-HISTORY-ERASE` owner's definition of done.

constraint: Widget click cannot bypass the Action Engine or the canonical owner; only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect
where: contract §6.3 I2(a) handles-as-nouns; §11 Gate 9 (fresh read at submission) and Gate 12 / APPROVAL path (`PENDING -> APPROVED -> COMPLETED`)
why: The load-bearing anti-staleness graft is applied at Gate 9 to the *widget submission's* frozen nouns. An approval-gated action is different: the ActionExecution is created at REQUEST_APPROVAL time with its arguments already resolved, and the approver's later tap moves the state machine to APPROVED, after which execution proceeds against arguments frozen minutes or hours earlier. The contract never states that the canonical owner re-resolves nouns at execute time on the approval path. So "the price shown 90 seconds ago is never the price charged" and "a slot someone else took cannot be committed" hold for direct commits and silently do not hold across the approval boundary — which is the path deliberately used for the highest-risk and largest-audience actions.
fix: Require the noun-resolution fresh read and SUPERSEDED/diff outcome at execute time on the approval path as well, not only at submission; if a noun has diverged since approval, the execution must return SUPERSEDED and re-enter approval with the diff rendered, rather than executing on stale values.

constraint: No BUTTON -> PROVIDER; widgets are never a system of record; only a final canonical confirmation causes a booking effect
where: contract open question 3 (`hold_token`, "a soft lock YClients does not own", specified as OPTIONAL/default-off) and §5.2 TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR `availability: Cell<'FREE'|'HELD'|'TAKEN'>`
why: The HELD state is already in the shipped body shape, so the mechanism is half-present rather than deferred. If `hold_token` is enabled, a tap on a selector — a kind whose ceiling is DRAFT and about which §11 Gate 11 says "no business effect is reachable from a selector" — creates a real occupancy effect on a single-salon calendar. Because the provider does not own the lock, the widget layer becomes the system of record for who holds a chair, which is the one thing the constraints forbid outright, and a phantom hold has no canonical owner to reconcile or expire it.
fix: Drop `hold_token` and rely on the SUPERSEDED-at-confirm outcome the handles-as-nouns graft already provides (the open question notes this is now cheap). Remove `HELD` from the availability enum unless and until the provider owns the hold, so the contract cannot express a lock nothing canonical holds.

constraint: UNKNOWN must never be rendered as failure (the Cell discipline the rest of the safety argument leans on)
where: contract §4.1 ("There is no bare number, string, boolean or date in any body field that reaches a user's eyes") against §5.1–5.2: `OptionItem.label/sublabel/badges`, `TableSpec.columns[].label`, `BOOKING_CONFIRMATION.lines[].label/detail` and `policy_notices`, `SETTINGS_DRAFT.diff[].from/to/effect_text`, `STRATEGY_OPTIONS.title/reasoning`, `FormField.label/help`, `SOURCE_STATUS.impact_text`, `LIMITATION.headline/detail`
why: The universal-Cell rule is stated absolutely and then contradicted by most of the contract's own bodies, including the fields most likely to be unknown at render time: a settings diff's `from`/`to` (where a missing prior value renders as empty or an em dash — both explicitly forbidden as UNKNOWN renderings), a confirmation line's `detail`, and a staff label in a masked schedule. The renderer conformance suite (M2, five branches per Cell) cannot protect a field that is not a Cell, and INV-4/INV-5 (`reason_code` and `unknowns_sentence` required for any non-KNOWN Cell) simply do not fire for bare fields, so the minted text equivalent will confidently omit an unknown it has no state for.
fix: Either make the rule real — convert every user-visible body field to `Cell<T>` and let the conformance suite and INV-4/INV-5 cover them — or narrow §4.1 to the fields it actually governs and add an explicit allowlist of server-authored constant strings, so implementers know which fields have no UNKNOWN protection.

constraint: This cycle: architecture only. 0 runtime changes, 0 production mutations.
where: section-migration-map.md §9 Phase 1 ("Honesty") and Phase 2 ("Tier A restorations"), read against section-packages-and-gate.md §11 ("Waves 2-6 are locked") and §5 (P22 is Wave 5)
why: Phase 1 schedules live production changes — rewriting /unsubscribe and /subscribe copy in `bot.py`/`privacy_policy.py`, replacing ~45 authority-dead Telegram replies with HANDOFF text, and removing the AI chat's gift-certificate offer — with the entry condition "immediately, in parallel with Phase 0". Phase 2 then ships two live consent surfaces whose entry condition is only "Phase 1 complete for the consent copy". Both sit inside the cycle the same document opens by declaring "0 runtime changes, 0 production mutations". They also contradict the package plan, which places the identical work in P28 (Wave 6) and P22 (Wave 5), both locked behind the Wave-1 exit gate, and which argues P20 must fence consent as HANDOFF-only *before* P22 exposes it. A reader following the migration map starts changing production this week; a reader following the packages plan does not touch production until a human approves the dossier. The two normative documents disagree about whether the fence is closed.
fix: Either (a) state explicitly that Phase 1/Phase 2 are a separately-authorised remediation lane that begins AFTER this cycle closes, with its own dated authorisation and its own rollback, or (b) delete the Phase 1/2 entry conditions and route the work through P22/P28 as the packages section already does. In both cases remove "immediately" and give every phase an entry condition that names the cycle boundary.

constraint: No old screen deleted before proven capability parity; the only mechanism that may authorise a deletion is INV-16, and it authorises nothing until green
where: section-authority-context-model.md Part A row 3 and "Summary of dispositions" (`localStorage.me_is_staff` → "DELETE FIRST, UNCONDITIONALLY, NO PARITY GATE", "Gate: none required"); section-migration-map.md §7.2 bucket B2 ("retire the entry point **immediately**", "Is it a parity claim? No")
why: Two deletions are authorised outside the gate by documents that each open by saying nothing they contain authorises a deletion. The contract §13 forbids "Removing any tab, route or command on the strength of this document" and the migration map says the parity gate is the only mechanism that may ever authorise one. The B2 exemption is additionally unsafe in its own terms: §7.1 says the Telegram authority finding is 2-of-3 verifiers with one dissent on causality and must be settled by a staging probe first, yet B2 retirement is scheduled ahead of that probe on the argument that the capability is already dead — which is the exact assumption §7.3 forbids ("never assume the capability is re-presented elsewhere without checking the HTTP surface case by case"). An exemption that anyone may claim by asserting "retiring changes nothing" is a hole in the only gate the programme has.
fix: Give both an explicit exception record rather than an exemption: a ledger row, a named owner, evidence that the surface grants nothing and carries no capability, and the same soak/rollback as any other row — just with G2/G4/G6 marked not-applicable and the reason cited. constraint: Chapter 10 NOT started; proactive may PRESENT EXISTING ALREADY-AUTHORIZED INFORMATION, it may not AUTONOMOUSLY INITIATE NEW BUSINESS STRATEGY
where: contract.md §2.3 `Origin.authority_basis`, §2.2 `WidgetSource`, §2.3 `ProactiveMoment` (includes `growth_plan`, `marketing_broadcast`, `owner_alert`), INV-11
why: "Presents already-authorized information" has no structural carrier. `authority_basis: 'pre_authorized_presentation'` is a single-value literal the emitter writes; INV-17 enforces only that the string is that string. So a scheduler may read live data, compose a growth plan nobody asked for, and emit it under a literal that asserts it was pre-authorized. constraint: Chapter 10 NOT started; no autonomous loop smuggled in through proactive behaviour

Start a C9 run, allocate reasoning budget")

constraint: Chapter 10 NOT started (proactive may not initiate); one normative answer per rule

constraint: No old screen deleted before proven capability parity

constraint: No old screen deleted before proven capability parity; ROLE REMOVAL FROM UX != ROLE REMOVAL FROM SECURITY

constraint: ROLE REMOVAL FROM UX != ROLE REMOVAL FROM SECURITY

constraint: ROLE REMOVAL FROM UX != ROLE REMOVAL FROM SECURITY

constraint: CHAT-FIRST != CHAT-ONLY: a fallback editor must exist for audit, exact configuration, accessibility and correction

Never from chrome"), §7 (empty state shows "three entry utterances") against decisions.json D4 (recommended option B: an authority-filtered capability index that composes an utterance)

constraint: CHAT-FIRST != CHAT-ONLY: a fallback editor must exist for audit, exact configuration, accessibility and correction

constraint: C6-C9 canonical business contracts unchanged; the chat-first UX must not require a C9 contract change; no second backend contract per widget
where: section-c9-c10-compat.md headline ("C9 compatibility PASS — Conditional on 7 corrections"; "STRATEGY_OPTIONS FAIL as written"; "APPROVAL PASS with 2 corrections"; "PROGRESS PASS with 1 correction") against the delivered contract.md, which applies essentially none of them
why: The design's own compatibility verdict is conditional on ten named corrections. The primary artefact carries the uncorrected text: (1) `Provenance.completeness` (contract §4.3) still omits `status: COMPLETE|PARTIAL|UNAVAILABLE`, which `c9Completeness` (c9.contract.ts:313-322) carries and `c9AgentResult` enforces via `c9Deny('false_completeness')`; (2) `facts_used` still drops `evidence_refs` and flattens `completeness` to `completeness?: number`, though c9.contract.ts:349-368 types it `evidence_refs: handles` (required) and `completeness: c9Completeness` (an object); (3) `four_eyes` is still present; (5) evidence handles are still presented as durable audit refs; (6) `Limitation.severity` still has no sourcing rule; (A) `approval_binding_echo` still echoes `ActionExecution.approvalBindingHash` rather than the `AiApprovalRequest.payloadHash` its own owner checks; (PROGRESS) `state` still includes `'failed'`, in a document that states "There is no `ERROR` kind and no `error` severity anywhere in this contract" (§5) and against a C9 step-state vocabulary that has no failed state. Consequence: §4.3's headline claim — "Mirrors `AgentResult@1` field-for-field so the composer copies rather than re-derives" — is verifiably false, and with it P3 ("completeness is copied, never recomputed") and INV-14's `completeness_envelope_hash` equality, which cannot hold between a lossy copy and a re-hash of the source.
fix: Apply the seven corrections into contract.md before review, or demote the compat section's verdict from PASS to CONDITIONAL-FAIL and say so in §14. At minimum, correct §4.3 so `facts_used` and `completeness` are byte-copies of the C9 shapes, delete `'failed'` from PROGRESS, and fix the approval hash reference.

constraint: Widgets must not promise a capability with no canonical owner (P2); AUTHORITY VALIDATION must be real, not asserted
where: contract.md:398 (`four_eyes: boolean` in `ConfirmationRequirement`), §11 Gate 12 ("Four-eyes and readback are enforced here, not in the UI"), section-migration-map.md §8 Tier C (`GAP-IDENTITY-TG-UNBIND`: "NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED, STEP_UP_VERIFIED, four-eyes"), against section-c9-c10-compat.md §3 ("Delete from the contract. No canonical source.")
why: I verified the repository: `grep -rn 'four_eyes|fourEyes' maya-saas-backend/src` returns zero hits, and `ai-tool-policy.service.ts:81-95 canDecide` is `approvalPolicy === 'actor'` → `requestedByUserId === principal.userId` (the requester IS the decider) and `'owner'` → any `OWNER_ROLES` member, the initiator included. There is no separation-of-duties enforcement anywhere. A widget that renders `four_eyes: true` states a control the platform does not have, and Gate 12 asserts it is "enforced here" when nothing enforces it. By the contract's own P2 this is the forbidden pattern — a promise with no owner — and the migration map makes the staff-Telegram-unbind restoration depend on it.
fix: Delete `four_eyes` from `ConfirmationRequirement` and from Gate 12's text, and rewrite the `GAP-IDENTITY-TG-UNBIND` row to name the actual approval policy (`owner`, initiator not excluded) or to carry a second `capability_gap_ref` for separation of duties.

constraint: Only a final canonical confirmation may cause a booking effect; risk/reversibility are copied from the canonical owner, never invented
where: contract.md §6.1 ("`risk_tier`, `reversible` and `audience_size` are **copied** from `proposed_action_intents[i]`") and §9.1 ladder step 8 ("a COMMIT action is permitted **only** when `risk_tier === 'low_write' && reversible === true`"), against c9.contract.ts:372-381
why: C9's `proposed_action_intents[]` element is `{capability, argumentHandles, risk: c9Enum('low_write','medium_write','high_write','restricted'), approval, reversibility: c9Enum('SOURCE_DEFINED'), rationale, audience_size}`. There is no boolean reversibility to copy — the only canonical value is the literal `'SOURCE_DEFINED'`, meaning the source owner decides and C9 does not know. The contract itself encodes this correctly in `AuthorityHint.reversibility: 'SOURCE_DEFINED'` and then contradicts it with `ConfirmationRequirement.reversible: boolean` described as copied. This is load-bearing because `reversible === true` is one of only two predicates gating the single most dangerous path in the whole design — a one-tap COMMIT actuated from a push notification by a CHANNEL_IDENTITY principal. The gate's input has no canonical source, so it will be authored at mint time by the same composer that wants the one-tap action. (Secondary: `risk` has no `'read'` member upstream, so a copied `risk_tier` can never legitimately be `'read'` — unstated.)
fix: Type `reversible` as `Cell<boolean>` sourced from the provider owner, defaulting to a non-KNOWN state, and make ladder step 8 require `state === 'KNOWN' && value === true`; or, preferably, delete the COMMIT exception from ladder step 8 entirely (see the platform section, which already caps `ANNOUNCEMENT` at NAVIGATE).

constraint: No second backend contract per widget; the LLM never generates numbers; a widget may not introduce a field its source capability cannot produce (P1/P3)
where: contract.md §5.2 STRATEGY_OPTIONS row ("reuses `c9Alternative` verbatim; NO_ACTION must be selectable (INV-13)") and INV-13 ("≤3 alternatives **and** a selectable NO_ACTION"), against c9.contract.ts:271-290, c9.store.ts:266-270, c9.strategy.ts:135
why: Verified against the repository: `c9Alternative` is `{key, title, kind: 'ACTION_PLAN'|'NO_ACTION', why, evidenceRefs, scopeHash, knownBenefit{factRefs, proposalText}, unknowns, risks, costSummary, approvalAdapterRefs, recommended}`. It has no `expected_effect`, no `risk_tier`, no `reversible` and no `audience_size` — so "reuses c9Alternative verbatim" is false, and `expected_effect: Measure` has no canonical source at all, forcing a model-authored number in direct violation of R2/INV-14. Worse, `c9.store.ts` validates `c9Array(c9Alternative, 3, 1)` — at most three IN TOTAL — and `c9.strategy.ts:135` executes `if (alternatives.length > 3) alternatives.length = 3;`, which truncates the NO_ACTION option away whenever three action plans are feasible. INV-13's "≤3 alternatives AND a NO_ACTION" is therefore unsatisfiable from a real run without synthesising an option the run does not contain. The compat section diagnosed both defects precisely and the primary artefact ships the uncorrected version.
fix: Adopt the compat section's amendment in the contract: `expected_effect: Cell<string>` sourced from `knownBenefit.proposalText` with `factRefs` as evidence (non-KNOWN when empty); source NO_ACTION from `review(optionKey:'c9.no_action')` when present and `review(accept:false)` otherwise; state that `recommended` is a label and never a pre-selection; and drop the "verbatim" claim.

constraint: No old screen deleted before proven capability parity; CHAT-FIRST != CHAT-ONLY
where: section-migration-map.md §2 ("There are 112 primary-navigation surfaces today and at most 63 rows dispositioned to leave primary navigation. Even if all 63 clear the gate, at least 49 primary-navigation entry points survive") and §9 Phase 7 ("at most 63 of 112 primary-nav entries darken. At least 49 remain"); section-packages-and-gate.md §2 ("112 primary-nav surfaces today, 63 dispositioned RETIRE — leaving 49... The completion gate therefore demands `<= 49`")
why: The subtraction assumes all 63 RETIRE FROM PRIMARY NAVIGATION rows are primary-nav surfaces. Joined against the evidenced inventory (ux-all-surfaces.json 795 rows, ux-all-dispositions.json 669 rows, matched by name), only **19** of the 63 RETIRE rows carry `primaryNav: true`; 44 do not, and 19 of those are `telegram-bot` surfaces that have no PWA primary navigation at all (channel split of the 63: pwa 38, telegram-bot 19, web-public 5, native-shell 1). Executing every assigned retirement leaves **93** primary-nav entries, not 49. Separately, 19 MERGE, 17 MOVE INTO CHAT WIDGET and 16 KEEP AS FULLSCREEN DETAIL rows ARE primary-nav and also displace an entry point, and 15 primary-nav surfaces are untriaged — none of them appear in the subtraction. So the number is wrong in both directions and is presented as "an arithmetic fact worth stating plainly". Most seriously, packages §8 turns it into a hard completion-gate threshold (`<= 49`) that the assigned dispositions cannot reach.
fix: Recompute from the ledger: count primary-nav rows by disposition, and define the gate threshold as `primaryNav surviving = 112 − (primary-nav rows in RETIRE ∪ MOVE ∪ MERGE that reached ENTRY_POINT_DARK)`. Restate §2 as "19 of the 112 are assigned RETIRE; a further 52 primary-nav rows are assigned MOVE/MERGE/FULLSCREEN and 15 are untriaged", and re-derive the gate number from that.

constraint: CHAT-FIRST != CHAT-ONLY; no old screen deleted before proven capability parity
where: section-information-architecture.md §0 ("**112 → 5.** Primary navigation shrinks from 112 reachable surfaces to five addressable destinations. 107 entry points leave primary navigation") against section-migration-map.md §9 Phase 7 ("At least 49 remain. That is the intended outcome") and section-packages-and-gate.md §2 ("takes primary navigation from 112 to 49... does not produce a chat-first shell. The inventory does not contain the decision that takes 49 to a handful") and decisions.json D2-primary-nav-shell (still an OPEN owner decision)
why: Three sections of one design give three incompatible answers to the same number, each stated as settled: 5 destinations (107 leave), 49 survivors ("that is the intended outcome"), and 49-with-the-real-decision-not-yet-made. Meanwhile decisions.json presents D2 as an unresolved question with options A/B/C for the owner. A reviewer cannot tell what the design actually proposes, and the two constraints at issue (no deletion before parity; chat-first is not chat-only) are adjudicated differently depending on which section is read. The IA's version is the one that would delete 107 entry points.
fix: Pick one and mark the others as derived. State in the IA that 5 is the *target* destination count pending D2 and that the *cycle* outcome is bounded by the parity ledger, not by the IA; state in the migration map and packages the same number the IA states. Any completion-gate threshold must cite the ledger, not a section headline.

constraint: Counts asserted in the design must be supported by the evidenced inventory
where: section-information-architecture.md §1 ("the PWA bundle contributes **41 enumerable primary-nav entry points** today" — 4+4+9+18+6 — "The balance of the 112 is contributed by the other channels (Telegram command menu, native shell, web-public)") and §11.7 ("The 112 → 5 arithmetic is exact on the count")
why: The evidenced inventory attributes **89** of the 112 `primaryNav: true` surfaces to channel `pwa`, and only 23 to every other channel combined (smm-bot 11, telegram-bot 5, public-web-auth 3, telegram-miniapp 2, web-public 1, public-community 1). The IA located 41 PWA entry points and attributed the remaining 71 to other channels; 48 PWA primary-nav surfaces are therefore unlocated by the section that opens with "A number like '112 → 5' is only honest if 'primary-nav item' has a test." §11.7's hedge covers the *allocation* but the claim "exact on the count" is about the composition, and the composition is wrong. Additionally, 11 of the 112 belong to `smm-bot` — a separate production system (`/opt/smm_bot`) — which the four shell destinations plainly do not absorb, so "107 entry points leave primary navigation" silently includes another product's navigation.
fix: Re-derive the 41 against the 89 pwa rows in ux-all-surfaces.json and publish the delta as ledger rows (they are the most likely place a capability is lost). Exclude non-MAYA-app channels (smm-bot in particular) from the 112 → 5 statement, or state explicitly that they are out of scope for the shell.

constraint: The accessibility contract must cover every widget type in the taxonomy; CHAT-FIRST != CHAT-ONLY (a fallback editor must exist for accessibility)
where: contract.md:512-515 (`a11y.role_hint` closed enum; `reading_order: string[] // option_ids / field keys`), INV-9 (contract.md:742), section-platform-and-channels.md §6.2 clauses A-1…A-16 and A-17
why: Read together, the a11y floor does not reach several kinds in the taxonomy. (1) `role_hint` has seven values and no member fits SCHEDULE (a two-dimensional lane/time grid with per-entry `intent_token`), PROGRESS (no `progressbar`), REPORT (a sectioned document), METRIC, BOOKING_CONFIRMATION, APPROVAL or SETTINGS_DRAFT — and none of the taxonomy's five extra kinds. (2) A-6 specifies a keyboard model only for `radiogroup`/`listbox`; no clause defines keyboard interaction for a schedule grid, for `TableSpec.row_intents`, or for a two-level `group_by` table, and NO clause anywhere covers data-table semantics (row/column headers, caption) despite CLIENT_LIST, REPORT and `CHART.table_equivalent` being the tabular kinds and WCAG 1.3.1 governing them. (3) A-3 requires `reading_order` to cover **every** interactive element, but the contract types it as option_ids / field keys — which excludes `SCHEDULE.entries[].intent_token`, `CLIENT_LIST.row_intents` and `bulk_intents`, `REPORT.fullscreen_intent`, `METRIC.drill_intent`, `CHART.export_intent`, `SETTINGS_DRAFT.apply/discard/editor_handoff_intent` and `BOOKING_CONFIRMATION.commit/amend/cancel`. A-3 and INV-9 are unsatisfiable as typed for at least eight of the seventeen kinds. (4) A-17 runs per emitted envelope; a `fullscreen_detail` is a route, not an envelope — so the surface whose declared reason is literally `'accessibility'`, the mandated non-chat fallback, is bound by no A11yFloor clause at all.
fix: Extend `role_hint` to cover grid/document/progressbar/link and add a clause per new value defining its keyboard model; add a data-table clause (headers, caption, group headers for `group_by`, row-intent activation); retype `reading_order` as a list of interactive-element refs (option_ids ∪ field_keys ∪ intent_tokens ∪ row/entry keys) so A-3 and INV-9 can be satisfied; and state normatively that a `fullscreen_detail` route renders envelopes and is bound by A-1…A-17.

constraint: The accessibility contract must genuinely cover the flows it claims (WCAG 2.2 AA is asserted as normative and CI-gated)
where: section-platform-and-channels.md §6.2 clause A-13 ("Any envelope carrying `flow_ttl_s` defaults to `on_expiry: 're_resolve'`, which discharges SC 2.2.1 structurally... Collapse-to-summary is permitted only where re-resolution is impossible, and then an extension affordance is required") against contract.md §8 Freshness regimes and §12 per-kind ceilings
why: The contract's own regimes contradict A-13's premise. `scenario` — explicitly "(booking, purchase, settings draft)" — is `flow_ttl_s: 1800` with `on_expiry: 'collapse_to_summary'`, not `'re_resolve'`. And the per-kind `expires_at` ceilings are TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR 90 s and BOOKING_CONFIRMATION 120 s. So the flagship booking flow both collapses rather than re-resolves and is capped at two minutes on the confirmation body — a hard time limit for a screen-reader, switch-access or motor-impaired user. A-13 then requires "an extension affordance" in exactly that case, and the contract defines none: there is no extension field, no `role: 'extend'`, no effect class and no intent in any body that extends a TTL. SC 2.2.1 is not discharged; it is asserted.
fix: Either set `on_expiry: 're_resolve'` for BOOKING_CONFIRMATION (and raise the 120 s ceiling accordingly), or add a first-class extension affordance — a `priority: 0`, undroppable `role: 'extend'` intent with `effect: 'REFINE'` that re-mints the confirmation from the canonical draft — and make A-13's CI check assert its presence on every envelope whose `on_expiry` is `'collapse_to_summary'`.

constraint: Do not create a second definition of the same artefact; the degradation ladder and the receipt are the instruments that prove nothing withheld is unreachable
where: contract.md §9 (`ChannelProfile`, `interaction_model: 'RICH'|'KEYBOARD'|'NOTIFICATION'|'SPEECH'|'TEXT_ONLY'|'NON_INTERACTIVE'`, flat `supports_*`) and §9.2 `RenderReceipt` (`applied_rules`, `dropped_intent_roles`, `degraded_to`, `truncation_disclosed`) against section-platform-and-channels.md §1.4-1.5 and §2 (seven render tiers `RICH_INTERACTIVE|RICH_CONSTRAINED|ANNOUNCEMENT|SPOKEN|TEXT_ONLY|PUBLIC_READ|ANONYMOUS_CHAT`, nested `supports {}`, `a11y_env`, and a `RenderReceipt` with `render_tier`, `intents_minted/emitted`, `intents_withheld[].reachable_via`, `body_reductions[].restored_by`, `escalation`)
why: Two mutually incompatible normative definitions of the same two named artefacts (`maya.channel.profile/1` and the RenderReceipt) exist in one design, with different member sets, different vocabularies and different shapes. Rule C4 — "nothing withheld is unreachable", described as "what makes aggressive degradation safe" — and conformance gates G1/G2/G10 are written against fields (`intents_withheld[].reachable_via`, `body_reductions[].restored_by`) that the contract's receipt does not have, so as delivered they cannot be evaluated. The divergence is also safety-relevant: contract ladder step 8 permits a COMMIT on a NOTIFICATION profile, while platform §2 caps `ANNOUNCEMENT` (web-push) at "`NAVIGATE` max". The primary artefact holds the permissive rule.
fix: Collapse to one definition in contract.md §9/§9.2 — take the platform section's richer receipt (it is the one C4 and G2 need) and its tier names — and delete the duplicate. Resolve the notification COMMIT question in favour of the stricter rule (NAVIGATE/HANDOFF only) in the surviving document.

constraint: Every channel that can deliver a widget must have a profile; the proactive scheduler is one of only three envelope minters
where: contract.md §8 Mint (minter 3 = "the proactive scheduler for the 12 canonical moments") and §9.1 ladder step 9 ("`NON_INTERACTIVE` (scheduler, email, SMS, social publishing, edge relay)") against section-platform-and-channels.md §1.4 `type ChannelId` (11 members) and §2 ("The seven render tiers, and the eleven channels on them")
why: The platform section's channel union is `pwa | native-shell | telegram-miniapp | telegram-bot | web-push | realtime-voice | guest-chat | web-public | public-community | sms | email` — 11 of the 17 evidenced channels. Missing: `scheduler` (32 surfaces), `smm-bot` (26), `edge-relay` (21), `backend` (7), `social-publishing` (7), `public-web-auth` (6) — 99 evidenced surfaces. The 7-tier table has no `NON_INTERACTIVE` tier at all, although `NON_INTERACTIVE` is a member of the contract's own `interaction_model` and is the target of ladder step 9. So the scheduler — a designated minter, and the carrier of all 12 proactive moments, all of which the inventory says any new chat UX must cover — has no registered profile, no tier and no fitting rule, and `G1 profile matrix` ("every envelope kind × 7 tiers") cannot cover the channel where proactive delivery actually happens.
fix: Add the six missing channels to `ChannelId` and give `NON_INTERACTIVE` a tier row with `max_intents: 0`, `NAVIGATE/HANDOFF` ceiling and a mandatory text-equivalent-plus-signed-link rendering; extend G1 to `kinds × tiers` including it.

constraint: Consent accept/decline is never a chat-rendered control actuated by channel identity alone; a widget may not promise a capability with no canonical owner (P2)
where: section-migration-map.md §8 Tier B, `GAP-CONSENT-REGISTER-EXPORT` ("Restored to: a `REPORT` widget with a top-3 summary card and a mandatory `fullscreen_detail: compliance.consent_register` + `export_intent`, delivered as an artefact into the conversation") against contract.md §6.8 NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED (which lists `consent.register.export`) and section-widget-taxonomy.md §9 ("`ARTIFACT` is emittable only for owner reports; the consent-register export has no owner")
why: Three internal contradictions on one row. (1) `consent.register.export` is on NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED, whose "only legal intent is HANDOFF" — yet the restoration home is a chat REPORT carrying an `export_intent` that delivers the Roskomnadzor journal into the transcript. That is precisely a chat-actuated control over a 152-FZ capability, and it also writes a register of identified data subjects into conversation history, which §8 Delete then makes erasable. (2) It relies on delivery "as an artefact", and ARTIFACT is not a kind the contract can express. (3) The taxonomy states this capability has no registered owner, so P2 forbids any intent at all until one exists — the migration map names an intent anyway. The gap ledger exists to prevent exactly this pattern (promising a remedy with no owner).
fix: Restate the row as: a `LIMITATION` with `capability_gap_ref: GAP-CONSENT-REGISTER-EXPORT` and no intent until the owner is registered; thereafter a `HANDOFF`-only entry to `fullscreen_detail: compliance.consent_register` behind `SESSION_VERIFIED`+, with the file delivered on the verified surface and never into the chat transcript.

constraint: No old screen deleted before proven capability parity — INV-16 is the only mechanism that may authorise a deletion
where: contract.md §12 INV-16 ("Every KEEP-disposition capability in the 669-disposition inventory has ≥1 of: a widget kind, a fullscreen route, a text intent") against the evidenced disposition split and section-migration-map.md §3
why: As worded in the primary artefact, INV-16 binds only KEEP-disposition rows. The evidenced inventory has two KEEP dispositions (KEEP AS CAPABILITY 201, KEEP AS FULLSCREEN DETAIL 76 = 277 rows). The 63 RETIRE FROM PRIMARY NAVIGATION rows — the only class that removes anything — plus 115 MOVE INTO CHAT WIDGET and 93 MERGE rows are outside the wording, as are the 126 surfaces with no disposition at all. So the gate that §0 and §13 describe as "the only mechanism that may ever authorise a deletion" does not, as written, cover the rows that delete. The migration map's §3 gate is correct and per-row (RETIRE binds G1–G9 plus a named successor in `parity_proven_by`); the contract's one-line restatement of it is narrower than the thing it gates, and the contract is the artefact CI will be written from.
fix: Rewrite INV-16 to bind every row whose terminal state removes an entry point or a surface — RETIRE, MOVE INTO CHAT WIDGET, MERGE — and to fail closed on any row whose disposition is UNTRIAGED, matching section-migration-map.md §3 and §1.5.

constraint: The eight no-route capabilities must EACH have a named restoration home
where: section-migration-map.md §8 Tier C `GAP-IDENTITY-TG-UNBIND` ("Restored to: the offboarding path, inside the same canonical transaction as membership deactivation. **Not a separate settings screen**") against ux-channels.json reconciliation entry 3 and contract.md §6.8 NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED
why: All eight gaps do have a named home — that check passes — but this one is restored in half. The evidenced capability is "Permanently detach a staff member's Telegram — **self-service unbind, AND** unlinking the Telegram identity from a MAYA account at offboarding", evidenced by `/unbind` being a handoff (bot.py:710-712), `master_unbind_yes/no` intercepted at bot.py:1699-1701 and `database.unbind_master` raising (database.py:1587-1589). The migration map restores only the offboarding transaction and explicitly refuses a self-service surface. The self-service half therefore has no named home and no remaining gap ref, so P2 will not fire for it either. Separately, `identity.client.channel.unbind` — one of the eight NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED entries, and a data-subject right, not an offboarding act — appears in no gap-ledger row and no restoration row anywhere in the migration map.
fix: Split the row: (a) offboarding unbind inside the membership transaction, AUTHORITY owner; (b) self-service staff unbind on a `STEP_UP_VERIFIED` shell surface; (c) add a ledger row and gap ref for `identity.client.channel.unbind` (client channel unlink) so P2 fires until it has an owner.

constraint: No BUTTON -> DATABASE BUSINESS MUTATION; the free-input surface must be rationed and countable
where: contract.md §5.2 B2 ("FORM is the only kind accepting free-form input and is therefore the designed leak; its emissions are counted per tenant per week") against contract.md:315 CHOICE body (`allow_free_text; free_text_hint?`) and §6.1 `InputSchema.fields.type` (`'string' | 'integer' | 'date' | 'time' | 'phone'` with only `max_len`/`pattern`)
why: The claim that FORM is the *only* free-form kind is false against the contract's own CHOICE body, which carries `allow_free_text`, and against `InputSchema`, which permits unbounded-domain scalar types on an intent of any kind (only `enum` and `ref` carry `enum_values`). The consequence is not stylistic: the per-tenant FORM emission counter — the design's stated (social) control on the free-input surface — does not observe the CHOICE free-text path or any `string`/`phone`/`integer`/`date` input on a non-FORM kind, so the one metric the design offers for its acknowledged leak under-counts it by construction. Ladder step 4 also escalates multi-select chains into FORM, further mixing the population the counter is meant to bound.
fix: Either remove `allow_free_text` from CHOICE (free text is a chat message, not a widget field) or extend the justification requirement and the emission counter to every envelope carrying a non-closed-domain input field, and say so in B2 instead of naming FORM as the only one.

constraint: Cross-document consistency of the restoration cost claim, which drives phasing
where: section-widget-taxonomy.md §9 ("**Two** of the eight ... are not greenfield builds") vs section-migration-map.md §8 Summary (Tier A 2 with live owner+ingress, Tier B 3 with owner but no ingress, Tier C 3 with none — i.e. five) vs section-packages-and-gate.md §2 ("**Six** of the eight 'restorations' are not greenfield")
why: Three different counts of the same fact in one design, each asserted as verified against the same worktree. The disagreement is not trivial: it moves `GAP-ATTRIBUTION-FIRST-TOUCH` and the two consent gaps between "promotion of an existing shadow owner" and "genuine build", and the phase assignment (2 / 4 / 8) and the D9 remediation-lane recommendation both rest on it. A reader cannot tell whether three, five or six of the eight already have owners.
fix: Publish one table, per gap, with three columns — canonical owner exists / ingress exists / route exists — each cell carrying a file:line. Derive every count in every section from that table.

constraint: Internal consistency of the normative document (the command path is the design's central safety claim)
where: contract.md:679 ("## 11. Command path — **eleven** gates") against the table immediately below it, which lists Gates 1 through 12, and against §12 INV-7/INV-8 and §13, which cite "Gate 12" as an operative step
why: The section heading miscounts its own gates. Gate 12 ("Canonical action — ActionEngine ... The Action Engine — never the widget, chat or renderer — calls the provider owner") is the single most safety-relevant step in the document and is the one the count drops. Anyone implementing from the heading, or auditing "did all eleven gates run", is working from a list that excludes the canonical-action gate.
fix: Retitle to "twelve gates" and check every downstream reference to the gate count.

constraint: A normative contract must not cite sections that do not exist
where: contract.md:350 (B2: "recorded as such in §17"), :537 (R3: "See §17 for what this does and does not accomplish"), :694 (Gate 8: "promotion criterion is an open question (§17)")
why: contract.md ends at §14 (Honest register). There is no §15, §16 or §17. Three normative clauses defer their justification, their limits and a promotion criterion to a section that was not written — including Gate 8's divergence-audit promotion criterion, which is the mechanism that would turn the shadow-mode intent-divergence check into an enforced refusal. The open-questions register those pointers imply (which a prior review cites for the `hold_token` question) is not in the artefact under review, so those deferrals are uncheckable.
fix: Either add §15–§17 (social controls, overlay limits, open questions with promotion criteria) or inline the three deferrals and delete the pointers.

constraint: Counts asserted about the consent/identity fence must be accurate
where: section-platform-and-channels.md §6.2 clause A-14 ("This constrains how the **six** `NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED` handoffs may be built") against contract.md:469-474, which lists eight
why: `NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED` has eight members: `consent.pd.grant`, `consent.pd.withdraw`, `consent.marketing.grant`, `consent.marketing.revoke`, `identity.staff.telegram.unbind`, `identity.client.channel.unbind`, `consent.register.export`, `conversation.history.erase`. The "six" in §6.8 is a different set (the six that map to gap-ledger entries). A-14 constrains how step-up authentication may be built for these handoffs; applying it to six of eight leaves two — including `consent.pd.grant` — outside the WCAG 3.3.8 constraint.
fix: Change "six" to "eight" in A-14 and make the CI check enumerate from the constant rather than from a prose number.

constraint: The shell must be derived by a rule, not by taste (the design's own standard); ROLE REMOVAL FROM UX != ROLE REMOVAL FROM SECURITY
where: section-information-architecture.md §2 L2 ("the contract's `NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED` list (8 entries) enumerates the acts that may never be a chat-rendered control... Grouped by the object they act on, those eight acts produce exactly four destinations. The shell is not a settings drawer that grew; it is *the handoff target set*, and it is closed for the same reason the widget-kind list is closed")
why: The derivation does not produce four. Grouped by object, the eight acts yield consent/privacy (`consent.pd.*`, `consent.register.export`, `conversation.history.erase`) → Privacy & Data; identity (`identity.staff.telegram.unbind`, `identity.client.channel.unbind`) → Connections; and at a stretch `consent.marketing.*` → Notifications. No NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED act lands on **Account**, which L2 justifies separately with prose ("who am I signed in as"). The claimed rule therefore produces at most three destinations and the fourth is a taste judgement presented as rule output — in a section whose stated virtue (and whose D2 recommendation reason) is that "A is the only option produced by a rule rather than by taste". D2 also remains an open owner decision.
fix: State the derivation honestly: three destinations follow from the handoff target set, Account is added for session identity, and the closure argument applies to the first three only. Or map an act to Account and show it.

constraint: The LLM's role must be bounded by a mechanism that exists
where: contract.md §8 Mint ("The LLM's role is bounded to `AgentResult@1.presentation_hint`: it may **propose** a kind; a server table `allowedKinds(capability) → WidgetKind[]` validates the proposal") against c9.contract.ts:384 (`presentation_hint: (v) => c9SafeText(v, 400)`, optional) and section-c9-c10-compat.md §3 ("Optional in the contract and **never emitted** by the released agent. No renderer may depend on it.")
why: `presentation_hint` is a free-form string of up to 400 characters with no enum and no kind vocabulary, it is optional in the C9 schema, and by the design's own repository reading the released agent never emits it. The contract presents it as the bounded channel through which the model influences presentation, which makes the bound sound structural when it is an unexercised, untyped, optional free-text field plus a validation table that does not yet exist. The `allowedKinds(capability)` table is named but specified nowhere.
fix: Say what is true: the model proposes nothing today; if a kind proposal is ever wanted, add a closed `presentation_kind_hint` enum to the widget layer's own projector input (not to C9) and specify `allowedKinds` as a normative table in the contract.

constraint: Replay and audit claims must be honest; UNKNOWN must never be rendered as failure
where: contract.md §8 Replay ("Because the envelope, the `RenderReceipt` and the receipts are all stored, any past interaction can be re-rendered in any profile for audit — including replaying an owner's Telegram interaction as its text equivalent for an inspector") and INV-4 ("every `KNOWN` Cell has non-empty `evidence_refs`") against section-c9-c10-compat.md §2 ("Handles live in an in-memory `Map` for one invocation. **A widget persisted in chat history holds handles that no longer resolve.**")
why: The design's own repository reading establishes that evidence handles are per-invocation and non-dereferenceable once stored, yet the contract makes non-empty `evidence_refs` the defining property of a KNOWN Cell and then claims full replay for audit. What can actually be replayed is the rendered text and the receipt; the evidential chain behind a KNOWN value cannot be re-walked from a stored envelope. The compat section's correction 5 ("Declare `evidence_refs` in a persisted envelope non-dereferenceable; evidence is re-read through a `REFINE` intent") is not in the contract.
fix: Add the compat section's correction 5 to §4.1/§4.3 and narrow the §8 Replay claim to "the rendered form and the receipt chain"; make any "show the evidence" affordance an explicit `REFINE` intent that re-reads, as the compat section specifies.
